scenarios.scenarioText: Reliable Technologies Pvt. Ltd., a closely held private company, received a written notice from the Registrar of Companies (ROC) requiring it to furnish information and explanation regarding certain inter-company transactions with its holding company. The directors were unsure how to respond and sought legal advice. During review, the ROC found the information insufficient and decided to conduct deeper scrutiny of the company's books of accounts.

questions.question: Under Section 206 of the Companies Act, 2013, when the Registrar issues a written notice requiring the company to furnish information, the time allowed to respond is:

options.A: A fixed period of 15 days from the date of notice
options.B: A fixed period of 30 days from the date of notice
options.C: Such time as may be specified in the notice
options.D: Not less than 7 days from the date of service

questions.explanation: Section 206(1) provides that the Registrar may, by a notice in writing, call upon the company to furnish in writing such information or explanation, within such time as may be specified in the notice.

questions.question: After examining the information furnished by Reliable Technologies Pvt. Ltd., the ROC was not satisfied with the explanation. Under Section 206(4), which action can the ROC take?

options.A: Directly file a criminal complaint before the Magistrate
options.B: Pass an order for winding up of the company on his own authority
options.C: After giving the company reasonable notice, inspect books himself or appoint one or more Inspectors
options.D: Refer the matter directly to SFIO without any further inquiry

questions.explanation: Section 206(4) empowers the Registrar, after giving reasonable notice to the company, to inspect the books of account and other books and papers of the company himself or appoint one or more inspectors for this purpose.

questions.question: The ROC appointed an Inspector who inspected the books of Reliable Technologies Pvt. Ltd. During inspection, the Inspector retained certain documents for further examination. Under Section 207, what is the initial period for which an Inspector can retain such books?

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 90 days
options.C: 180 days
options.D: 365 days

questions.explanation: As per Section 207(2), the Inspector can retain the books of account and other books and papers for a period not exceeding 180 days at a time. After 180 days, it may be extended for a further period not exceeding 180 days with prior approval of the authority that appointed the Inspector.

questions.question: After completing the inspection of Reliable Technologies Pvt. Ltd., the Inspector prepared his report. Under Section 208, which of the following statements about the Inspector's report is CORRECT?

options.A: The report is confidential and cannot be used as evidence in any court of law
options.B: The report must be submitted to the NCLT, which then forwards it to the Central Government
options.C: The report submitted to the Central Government is admissible as evidence in legal proceedings
options.D: The company has a right to access the full report before it is submitted to the Central Government

questions.explanation: Section 208(2) provides that the report of any Inspector appointed under this Chapter shall be admissible as evidence in any legal proceedings. The report is submitted to the Central Government (not NCLT), and there is no mandatory right for the company to see the report before submission.

scenarios.scenarioText: Following widespread media reports about large-scale financial irregularities at Prestige Constructions Ltd., a listed public company, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs received multiple complaints from investors and creditors. The Central Government, after preliminary inquiry, found circumstances suggesting that the company's business was being conducted with intent to defraud its creditors and investors. The investigation was subsequently assigned to the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO).

questions.question: Under Section 210 of the Companies Act, 2013, the Central Government can order an investigation into the affairs of a company. Which of the following is NOT a valid ground for ordering such an investigation?

options.A: The company has passed a special resolution requesting investigation
options.B: The Tribunal, in the course of any proceeding before it, has ordered investigation
options.C: The company has failed to file its annual returns for two consecutive years
options.D: The Central Government is of the opinion, based on information received, that the business is being conducted fraudulently

questions.explanation: Section 210 provides for CG-ordered investigation on three grounds: (a) special resolution by the company, (b) Tribunal's order, or (c) CG's own opinion based on circumstances or information. Non-filing of annual returns is a separate default not covered under Section 210.

questions.question: Once the SFIO takes up the investigation of Prestige Constructions Ltd. under Section 212, which of the following statements is CORRECT regarding other investigating agencies?

options.A: The ROC may simultaneously continue its own inspection initiated before SFIO was assigned
options.B: No other investigating agency of the Central Government shall investigate the affairs of the company
options.C: The company's statutory auditors are automatically suspended from performing their duties
options.D: The company's board of directors must resign immediately upon SFIO assignment

questions.explanation: Section 212(2) specifically provides that where SFIO investigates any offence under this Act, no other investigating agency of the Central Government or any State Government shall proceed with investigation in such case. All ongoing investigations are transferred to SFIO.

questions.question: Under Section 212 of the Companies Act, 2013, offences covered in an SFIO investigation are treated as:

options.A: Compoundable and bailable
options.B: Non-compoundable but bailable
options.C: Cognizable and non-bailable
options.D: Cognizable but bailable at the discretion of the court

questions.explanation: Section 212(6) provides that notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the offences covered under an SFIO investigation shall be cognizable and non-bailable. This makes it harder for accused persons to obtain bail.

scenarios.scenarioText: Galaxy Pharmaceuticals Ltd. is a listed public company having a share capital of ₹10 crores, divided into 1,00,000 equity shares with 8,000 registered members. A group of 120 members filed an application before the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) alleging mismanagement and large-scale fraud by the promoter directors, who were siphoning off company funds through fictitious subsidiaries. The NCLT is considering whether to order a formal investigation.

questions.question: Under Section 213 of the Companies Act, 2013, for a company having share capital, what is the minimum number of members required to make a valid application to the Tribunal for ordering an investigation?

options.A: Not less than 200 members or 1/5th of total members, whichever is less
options.B: Not less than 100 members or 1/10th of total members, whichever is less
options.C: Not less than 50 members or 1/5th of total members, whichever is more
options.D: Not less than 100 members or 1/5th of total members, whichever is more

questions.explanation: Section 213(a) provides that the Tribunal may order investigation on application of not less than 100 members, or members holding not less than 1/10th of the total number of members — whichever is less. In Galaxy's case, 1/10th of 8,000 = 800. Since 100 is less, the threshold is 100 members.

questions.question: The 120 members of Galaxy Pharmaceuticals Ltd. filed their application before the NCLT. What is the security deposit they must furnish along with the application under Section 213?
questions.explanation: Section 214 requires that no application shall be made to the Tribunal unless the applicant deposits such security for payment of costs and expenses as may be prescribed. The prescribed security deposit under the rules is ₹25,000.

questions.question: After examination, the NCLT found that the application filed by the 120 members of Galaxy Pharmaceuticals Ltd. was vexatious and not supported by genuine concerns. What order can the NCLT pass in such a case?

options.A: Order the applicant members to pay costs to the company, not exceeding ₹1 lakh
options.B: Dismiss the application and order no further action
options.C: Refer the matter to the ROC for a preliminary investigation
options.D: Pass no specific order — the Tribunal can only order investigation, not costs

questions.explanation: If the Tribunal finds that the application was frivolous or vexatious, it may after hearing the applicant, by order make the applicant liable to pay costs to the company up to ₹1 lakh. This is a deterrent against frivolous petitions.

scenarios.scenarioText: An Inspector was appointed by the Central Government to investigate the affairs of Monarch Steel Ltd. following an anonymous complaint. During the investigation, the Inspector summoned the company's statutory auditor, legal advisor, banker, and several employees to produce documents and give statements. Each party raised different objections about the scope of the Inspector's powers and their obligations to cooperate.

questions.question: Under Section 217 of the Companies Act, 2013, when an Inspector calls upon any officer, employee, or agent of the company to appear before him, the person is bound to:

options.A: Appear only if he is a current director or officer of the company
options.B: Appear and answer questions but is not bound to produce physical documents
options.C: Appear, answer questions on oath, and produce all such books, documents and records as required
options.D: Appear only if a separate court order for each person is obtained

questions.explanation: Section 217(1) gives inspectors powers of a civil court for purposes of the inspection, including summoning and enforcing attendance of any person and examining them on oath, and compelling production of documents. All officers, employees, agents, bankers, auditors, and legal advisors of the company are bound to assist the Inspector.

questions.question: The company's legal advisor refused to produce certain written communications exchanged with Monarch Steel Ltd., claiming legal professional privilege. Under Section 227 of the Companies Act, 2013, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

options.A: Legal advisors must produce all communications with the company without any exception
options.B: Legal advisors are not compelled to disclose any privileged communication made to them in that capacity
options.C: Legal professional privilege applies only in criminal proceedings, not in company law investigations
options.D: The Inspector can override legal privilege with a special order from the Central Government

questions.explanation: Section 227 expressly provides that nothing in this Chapter shall compel any legal advisor to disclose any privileged communication made to him in that capacity. Legal professional privilege is fully protected and the Inspector cannot override this protection.

questions.question: The banker of Monarch Steel Ltd. was summoned and refused to provide details about the company's accounts, citing banking secrecy obligations. Under Section 227, which statement is CORRECT regarding the banker's position?

options.A: Bankers are completely exempt from any obligation to disclose customer information to an Inspector
options.B: Bankers can be compelled to disclose information relating to the company's affairs only if the Tribunal makes a specific direction in this regard
options.C: Bankers must mandatorily disclose all account information to the Inspector without requiring any Tribunal order
options.D: Bankers may be compelled by the Central Government to disclose information, but not by an Inspector

questions.explanation: Section 227 provides that nothing in this Chapter shall compel a banker to disclose any information as to the affairs of any of their customers other than such company, unless the Tribunal directs that such information shall be disclosed. So banker protection exists but can be overridden by Tribunal direction.

questions.question: An employee of Monarch Steel Ltd. refused to answer certain questions put by the Inspector, claiming the questions were irrelevant to the investigation. What are the legal consequences of such refusal under Section 217?

options.A: The Inspector can impose a penalty of ₹50,000 on the spot for non-cooperation
options.B: The employee shall be punishable with imprisonment up to 6 months under the Companies Act
options.C: The person refusing shall be liable as if he were guilty of contempt of court
options.D: The Inspector can only report the refusal to the CG, who may take enforcement action later

questions.explanation: Section 217(7) provides that any person who refuses to answer the questions put to him by the Inspector, or refuses to produce any book or document, shall be punishable as if he were guilty of contempt of court. This gives the investigation teeth and ensures compliance.

scenarios.scenarioText: During the investigation of Pacific Traders Ltd., the Inspector discovered critical financial documents that appeared to be in danger of being tampered with, removed, or destroyed by certain employees. He applied to the Central Government for permission to seize these documents. Separately, following submission of the Inspector's interim report revealing massive asset misappropriation, the company's assets were sought to be protected through court orders.

questions.question: Under Section 220 of the Companies Act, 2013, an Inspector can seize documents or books of the company only with prior approval of:

options.A: The NCLT alone, regardless of who appointed the Inspector
options.B: The Central Government or the Tribunal, depending on under whose authority the investigation was ordered
options.C: The Serious Fraud Investigation Office in all cases
options.D: The Registrar of Companies after obtaining a Magistrate's order

questions.explanation: Section 220 provides that an Inspector shall not seize any books and papers unless he has obtained prior approval from the Central Government (if he was appointed by CG) or the Tribunal (if appointed by Tribunal). The appropriate authority depends on who ordered the investigation.

questions.question: After seizing documents from Pacific Traders Ltd., the Inspector must return them within what time period under Section 220?

options.A: 30 days, extendable by another 30 days with fresh approval
options.B: 90 days, which is not extendable under any circumstances
options.C: 180 days, extendable by a further period not exceeding 180 days with prior approval
options.D: 365 days from the date of seizure, with no extension permitted

questions.explanation: Section 220(2) requires the Inspector to return the books and papers seized within 180 days of seizure. This period may be extended with the prior approval of the authority under which the Inspector was appointed, for a further period not exceeding 180 days.

questions.question: The NCLT was approached to freeze the assets of Pacific Traders Ltd. based on the Inspector's interim report. Under Section 221, the NCLT can pass a freezing order if:

options.A: Only after the Inspector has submitted his final report confirming fraud beyond reasonable doubt
options.B: The Tribunal is satisfied on the basis of the Inspector's report that there are adequate reasons to freeze the assets
options.C: The company has already been declared insolvent under the IBC, 2016
options.D: The Central Government passes a specific notification authorising the NCLT to freeze assets

questions.explanation: Section 221 empowers the Tribunal to make an order (i) restraining disposal of any assets of a company or its related entities, or (ii) freezing assets of the company, if it is satisfied on the basis of the Inspector's report that there is adequate reason to do so. Interim report is sufficient — final report is not required.

questions.question: The NCLT issued a restraint order against Pacific Traders Ltd. under Section 222. Which of the following transactions would be PROHIBITED without prior NCLT approval under such an order?

options.A: Payment of salaries and statutory wages to employees
options.B: Transfer of shares by any member, or disposal of any asset of the company
options.C: Filing of statutory returns and compliance forms with the ROC
options.D: Payment of statutory dues such as TDS, GST and other taxes

questions.explanation: Section 222 empowers the Tribunal to pass a restraint order directing that no transfer of shares or disposal of any asset of the company shall take place without the prior approval of the Tribunal. Routine operational payments like salaries and taxes are not affected by this order.

scenarios.scenarioText: After completing a two-year investigation of Pinnacle Infrastructure Ltd., the Inspector submitted his comprehensive report to the Central Government. The report revealed serious irregularities including large-scale misappropriation of ₹500 crores by promoter directors, creation of fictitious assets, and systematic fraud against minority shareholders and creditors. The Central Government is now deliberating on the appropriate course of action based on the Inspector's findings.

questions.question: Under Section 223 of the Companies Act, 2013, regarding the Inspector's Report, which of the following is CORRECT?

options.A: The Inspector must submit only a single final report; submission of interim reports is not permitted
options.B: The Inspector may and shall submit interim report(s) as well as a final report to the Central Government
options.C: The final report must be simultaneously submitted to the company and the Central Government
options.D: The Inspector's report must be submitted to the NCLT which then presents it to the Central Government

questions.explanation: Section 223(1) provides that the Inspector shall, and if directed by the Central Government shall, submit interim reports to the Central Government and on conclusion of the investigation, shall submit a final report. Interim reports are expressly contemplated under the law.

questions.question: In subsequent legal proceedings against the promoter directors of Pinnacle Infrastructure Ltd., the prosecutor sought to admit the Inspector's report as evidence. This was challenged by the defense. The Inspector's report is admissible because:

options.A: An Inspector is a government officer and therefore his findings are legally conclusive against the company
options.B: Section 223(2) specifically provides that the Inspector's report is admissible as evidence
options.C: Evidence of this type is always admissible under the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 without qualification
options.D: The company had agreed during the investigation process that the report could be used as evidence

questions.explanation: Section 223(2) expressly provides that the report of any Inspector appointed under Chapter XIV shall be admissible in any legal proceeding as evidence in relation to any matter contained therein. The report is not conclusive but is admissible evidence.

questions.question: Based on the Inspector's report revealing massive fraud at Pinnacle Infrastructure Ltd., what actions can the Central Government take under Section 224?

options.A: Only petition for winding up — the court handles all criminal and civil remedies independently
options.B: Only file a criminal complaint — civil remedies like winding up must be pursued separately
options.C: Present a petition for winding up, file a complaint for prosecution, apply to NCLT for relief, or direct recovery of assets
options.D: Directly impose penalties on the directors without any court proceedings

questions.explanation: Section 224 gives multiple concurrent options to the CG: (a) present a petition for winding up, (b) file a complaint in court for any offence, (c) apply to the Tribunal for any appropriate relief against the company or its officers, or (d) arrange for disgorgement/recovery of assets fraudulently acquired.

questions.question: The investigation expenses incurred by the Central Government in the Pinnacle Infrastructure Ltd. case amounted to ₹2 crores. After a promoter director was convicted for the fraud discovered during the investigation, what happens to these investigation expenses under Section 225?

options.A: The expenses are permanently written off as routine government expenditure
options.B: The expenses are recoverable from the convicted person as a civil debt due to the Central Government
options.C: The company must compulsorily reimburse the Central Government regardless of any conviction
options.D: The NCLT determines on a case-by-case basis whether investigation expenses are recoverable

questions.explanation: Section 225(3) provides that where any person is convicted on a prosecution instituted as a result of the Inspector's report, the expenses of the investigation shall be recoverable from the convicted person as a civil debt due to the Central Government. This creates a personal liability on the convicted fraudster.

scenarios.scenarioText: Cosmos Trading Ltd. was under active SFIO investigation when its shareholders, due to unrelated business difficulties, passed a special resolution for voluntary winding up. Simultaneously, the Central Government was separately investigating the beneficial ownership structure of Nova Holdings Ltd., where it suspected that certain foreign entities were exercising covert control over the company's affairs in violation of regulatory norms. During the investigation of Nova Holdings, the Central Government was considering appointing a firm of chartered accountants as the Inspector.

questions.question: After Cosmos Trading Ltd. passed a resolution for voluntary winding up, what is the effect on the ongoing SFIO investigation under Section 226?

options.A: Voluntary winding up automatically terminates any ongoing investigation as the company ceases to exist
options.B: The investigation continues undisturbed — Section 226 provides that voluntary winding up shall not affect or stop the investigation
options.C: The investigation is suspended and can only continue after fresh approval from the Central Government
options.D: The Inspector must apply to NCLT within 30 days to obtain permission to continue the investigation

questions.explanation: Section 226 expressly provides that the voluntary winding up of a company shall not affect or stop the investigation directed under this Chapter. The legislature deliberately ensured that companies cannot escape investigation by opting for voluntary winding up.

questions.question: The Central Government is investigating the ownership structure of Nova Holdings Ltd. under Section 216. What is the PRIMARY purpose of an investigation ordered under Section 216?

options.A: To investigate whether the company has committed fraud against its secured creditors
options.B: To ascertain the persons who are or have been financially interested in the success or failure of the company or who are able to control or materially influence its policy
options.C: To identify members who have transferred shares in violation of SEBI insider trading regulations
options.D: To investigate the company's related party transactions for violations under Section 188

questions.explanation: Section 216(1) empowers the CG to appoint an Inspector to investigate and report on the membership of any company, and otherwise with respect to the company, for the purpose of determining the true persons who are or have been financially interested in the success or failure of the company or who are able to control or materially influence its policy.

questions.question: The Central Government was considering appointing a reputed firm of chartered accountants as the Inspector for investigating Nova Holdings Ltd.'s ownership structure. Under Section 215, which restriction applies to such an appointment?

options.A: An Inspector must mandatorily be a practising advocate of at least 10 years standing
options.B: A firm or body corporate shall not be appointed as an Inspector under this Chapter
options.C: The Inspector must be a serving IAS or IPS officer of Joint Secretary rank or above
options.D: Any Inspector appointed must first obtain prior clearance from SEBI before commencing investigation

questions.explanation: Section 215 provides that a firm or body corporate shall not be appointed as an Inspector under this Chapter. Only an individual person can be appointed as an Inspector. This ensures personal accountability and prevents diffusion of responsibility that would occur if a corporate entity were to act as Inspector.
